# U.S. Indian Affairs

> > The Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) enhances quality of life and economic opportunities for American Indians and Alaska Natives through federal programs, trust fund management, education, and nation-to-nation tribal engagement.

The BIA operates under the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Indian Affairs within the Department of the Interior, managing federal trust responsibilities for federally recognized tribes through regional offices, the Bureau of Indian Education, and specialized bureaus. The site provides comprehensive policy documentation, operational guidance, and tribal consultation resources.

## Key Topics

- Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA)
- Bureau of Indian Education (BIE)
- Indian Affairs Manual (IAM)

- Tribal Consultation & Engagement

## Organizational Structure & Leadership

- [U.S. Indian Affairs](https://www.bia.gov): BIA homepage: mission to enhance quality of life and economic opportunities for American Indians and Alaska Natives.
- [Office of the Assistant Secretary for Indian Affairs](https://www.bia.gov/as-ia): Overview of Assistant Secretary for Indian Affairs office and federal trust responsibilities.
- [Bureau of Indian Affairs](https://www.bia.gov/bia): BIA bureau overview covering mission, governance, and federal programs for tribes.
- [Leadership](https://www.bia.gov/leadership): BIA leadership team including Assistant Secretary for Indian Affairs.
- [White House Council on Native American Affairs](https://www.bia.gov/whcnaa): WHCNAA: interagency coordination for Native American policy and language revitalization.

## Core Bureaus & Services

- [Bureau of Indian Education (BIE)](https://www.bia.gov/bie): BIE overview: federal education policy and indigenous schools administration.
- [Bureau of Trust Funds Administration](https://www.bia.gov/btfa): BTFA overview: trust fund management and fiduciary responsibilities for tribal assets.
- [Programs and Services](https://www.bia.gov/programs-services): Overview of BIA programs including education, economic development, and natural resources.
- [Regional Offices](https://www.bia.gov/regional-offices): BIA regional offices and 83 agencies providing services to federally recognized tribes.

## Policy & Procedures Documentation

- [Indian Affairs Manual](https://www.bia.gov/policy-forms/manual): Indian Affairs Manual (IAM): permanent operational policies for IA programs.
- [Indian Affairs Directives System](https://www.bia.gov/directives-system): IA Directives System: policies, procedures, and administrative guidance documentation.
- [IA Handbooks](https://www.bia.gov/policy-forms/handbooks): IA Handbooks: detailed procedures implementing IAM policies for employees.
- [Memoranda](https://www.bia.gov/policy-forms/memoranda): National Policy Memoranda (NPM): interim instructions for IA employee duties.
- [Regional Directives](https://www.bia.gov/policy-forms/regional-directives): Regional directives implementing IAM policy at BIA regional offices.
- [Assistant Secretary's Orders (ASO)](https://www.bia.gov/policy-forms/assistant-secretarys-orders): Assistant Secretary's Orders: delegations of authority and organizational directives.

## Tribal Consultation & Engagement

- [Tribal Consultations](https://www.bia.gov/service/tribal-consultations): Tribal consultation and engagement: nation-to-nation relationship and regulatory affairs.
- [Upcoming Tribal Consultation Sessions](https://www.bia.gov/as-ia/consultations-listening-sessions/schedule): Schedule of upcoming tribal consultation and listening sessions.
- [Current Rulemakings](https://www.bia.gov/as-ia/raca/current-rulemakings): Current federal rulemaking including ISDEAA, STOP Act, and mineral estate regulations.

## Forms & Resources

- [Online Forms](https://www.bia.gov/policy-forms/online-forms): IA and BIE online forms directory including Paperwork Reduction Act forms.

## Optional

- [Current Year's News](https://www.bia.gov/news): Press releases and news updates on tribal affairs, education, and federal policy.
